report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of forest.py; verified node kind discrimination, edge construction, and type/document layer gating against the code present.
risks: line 285-295 | medium | Node kind discrimination uses attributes dict but module['kind'] may not exist; defaults to 'source_file' | Verify that modules dict always has 'kind' key or handle missing gracefully.

line 355-360 | low | Type edge source gate allows module_ids and type_ids; if a type node id accidentally in module_ids, it's skipped; could lose legitimate edges | Confirm that type ids never collide with module ids upstream.
line 375-380 | medium | Temporal pair dedup uses sorted((a,b)) but a and b are strings; if ids differ only by case, sorting may not be consistent | Ensure ids are case-sensitive or add normalization.

claims.text: This module's own docstring already said documents could be added 'as new node kinds and relation layers without changing this contract', and this is that, in full: one discriminator read, no new field, no new dataclass, no schema bump.
claims.why: The code reads attributes.get('kind') and sets kind to 'document' or 'source_file'; no new dataclass, no schema bump. The docstring claim is satisfied by this code.

claims.text: heat_score/churn come out 0 because documents are held out of module_heat upstream, which is deliberate, not missing data.
claims.why: The code updates attributes with heat_score and churn from heat_by_module; if module not in heat_by_module, defaults to 0. Document nodes get kind 'document' but heat data comes from module; if documents are not in module_ids, they won't be in heat_by_module, so heat_score=0. The claim is consistent with the code.

claims.text: type_ids is a SEPARATE set from module_ids on purpose, and this is the single most load-bearing line of the addition. module_ids is not a convenience variable: it is the membership gate of four other layers (imports, document links, co-change and clone-hyperedge members). Widen it and a type node becomes eligible to be a clone-group member or an import endpoint, which is a fabricated fact about the repository, not a cosmetic leak. So type nodes get their own set, and every gate below names exactly the sets it accepts.
claims.why: The code defines type_ids as a separate set. Later gates: imports (line 345) checks source and target in module_ids, not type_ids; document links (line 365) checks module_ids; co-change (line 390) checks module_ids; clone hyperedges (line 400) checks member in module_ids. Type nodes are excluded from those layers. The claim is verified.

claims.text: Absent key -> empty loop -> byte-identical forest, so an index built without the type layer produces the forest it always produced.
claims.why: The code uses index.get('type_nodes') or (), which returns empty iterable if key absent. The loop over type_rows will be empty, and type_ids remains empty. No type nodes added. The forest is identical to one without type layer.

claims.text: Three refusals, none of them redundant: a row that is not one of the two type kinds is not this layer's business; an id in the namespace of files would collide with a real file in build_forest_hierarchy (which raises on two ids mapping to one path) and is refused rather than renamed; and an id outside the type:/field: namespace cannot be told apart from a path by any downstream reader.
claims.why: The code checks: (1) kind not in _TYPE_NODE_KINDS -> continue; (2) not _is_type_node_id(node_id) or node_id in module_ids -> continue; (3) node_id in type_ids -> continue. These match the three refusals. The claim is fully supported.

claims.text: A separate relation, not extra imports edges: the multiplex graph exists so two kinds of relation can coexist without either one being read as the other. A link says 'this document refers to that file'; an import says 'this code cannot run without that file'. Merging them would silently move fan_in and every reachability answer derived from the import layer, including the safety fence's dominance fraction.
claims.why: The code creates edges with relation 'documents' (line 370), separate from 'imports' (line 351). The comment explains the rationale; the code implements separation.

claims.text: Absent key -> empty loop -> byte-identical forest, so an index built without documents produces the forest it always produced.
claims.why: The code uses index.get('document_links') or (), so if key absent, loop is empty. No document edges added. Forest unchanged.

claims.text: The endpoint gate is asymmetric and that is not an oversight: a TARGET is always a type-kind node, while a SOURCE may also be a file, because consumes/produces start at a FUNCTION and functions are not forest nodes -- so those two attach to the file that declares the function and carry its identity in attributes['function_ref'].  Anything else is dropped in silence rather than manufactured: an edge to a type node the index did not publish is missing evidence, and inventing the endpoint would make the forest disagree with the index it was normalised from.
claims.why: The code checks target not in type_ids -> continue; source not in module_ids and source not in type_ids -> continue. So target must be type node, source can be module or type. The claim is consistent.

claims.text: Deduplicated on the FULL row, not on the pair: one function can legitimately consume the same type twice through two different parameters, and collapsing those two would delete the param evidence that makes the edge worth publishing.
claims.why: The dedup key includes relation, source, target, and _canonical_key(attributes). So two rows with same source, target, relation but different attributes (e.g., different param) are kept. The claim is verified.

claims.text: Two byte-identical rows, on the other hand, are one fact stated twice.
claims.why: If two rows have identical source, target, relation, and attributes (canonical key same), they will have same key and second is skipped. The claim is consistent.

observations.what: Node kind discrimination for modules uses attributes dict which may not have 'kind' key; defaults to 'source_file' if missing.
Type node id check uses _is_type_node_id and also checks node_id not in module_ids; if a type node id accidentally collides with a module id, it is skipped (not refused with error).
Temporal pair dedup uses sorted((a, b)) after converting to strings; if a and b are identical after sorting, they are considered same pair regardless of original order.
Hyperedge weight calculation uses cluster.get('similarity') or cluster.get('shared_runs') or cluster.get('count') or 1.0; order of precedence may affect weight.
Provenance includes 'backend', 'scope_key', 'ignored', 'tokenizer' from index; no validation that these keys exist or have correct types.
